name: The Lantern Keeper
description: An elderly woman in a weathered gray hood, carrying a lantern that burns without oil. She watches you the way one watches a candle that should have gone out.

nodes.text: 'So the ash gives back its captain.' She lifts the lantern; amber light finds the Warden crest on your chest. 'You wake with a sword you did not earn and a fire in your chest that will not go out. I have waited a long while to see which of those you trust.'

options.label: What is this fire inside me?

nodes.text: 'A keeper of lanterns and of names. I was here when the bells rang seven times; I am still here, which is either devotion or a failure to be thorough. The hood is for the wind, not for mystery.'

'Veyrath tried to buy forever and paid with everything else. The court says the Wardens broke the kingdom — read their proclamations, they are very proud of that sentence. The court lies, Warden. Lie loudly enough and long enough and the dead will repeat it for you.'

options.label: How do I know you are telling the truth?

nodes.text: 'You do not. Truth is not a lantern — it does not light itself. Walk. Look at what the bells left behind, and at who profited. Seven memories of yours went into the ash; gather them, and then call me a liar to my face.'

'The last ember of the Ashen Flame, folded into a Warden's chest. It kept you from the grave, and it will keep you from rest until it is spent. Guard it — or let it use you as the king meant to use you. A vessel that forgets it is a vessel ends up on a throne it cannot leave.'
